description: A wrapper that responds to touches without providing visual feedback. Use only if you have a very specific reason. All touchable elements should ideally provide feedback to the user.
usageNotes: Supports only one child; for multiple children, wrap them in a View
Works by cloning its child and passing responder props; intermediary components must forward these props
Better to use Pressable for modern touch handling with feedback

delayLongPress.description: Duration (ms) from onPressIn before onLongPress is called

delayPressIn.description: Duration (ms) from the start of touch before onPressIn is called

delayPressOut.description: Duration (ms) from touch release before onPressOut is called

hitSlop.description: Defines how far touch can start away from the button

pressRetentionOffset.description: Distance off the button touch may move before deactivating (e.g., when ScrollView is disabled)

onPress.description: Called when touch is released (not if cancelled)

onLongPress.description: Called if touch lasts longer than delayLongPress

onPressOut.description: Called immediately when touch is released

onFocus.description: Called when the element receives focus

onBlur.description: Called when the element loses focus

onLayout.description: Called on mount and layout changes

nativeID.description: Used to locate this view from native code

id.description: Alternative identifier with precedence over nativeID

touchSoundDisabled.description: Android only: disables system sound on touch

notes: TouchableWithoutFeedback is mostly used for dismissing keyboards or other invisible touches
All touchable elements should ideally provide visual feedback
Better to migrate to Pressable for modern React Native projects
